answer.generated: Virtual memory acts as an intermediate layer between physical memory and machine memory, allowing the operating system to map virtual addresses to real addresses. This mapping is done using page tables, which translate virtual memory into real memory, enabling efficient use of physical memory resources. In a virtual machine environment, the VMM further maps guest virtual memory to host physical memory, providing isolation and flexibility. Thus, virtual memory bridges the gap between abstract logical addresses and concrete hardware addresses, supporting larger address spaces than available physical memory.
